meta.title: Software that runs itself
meta.description: Autofract is an independent studio building antifragile AI systems — self-healing infrastructure, autonomous video production, a tamper-evident price record, and open-data products. 100+ services in production.

hero.sub: An independent studio building antifragile AI systems. Four production platforms. 100+ services. Zero dashboards to babysit.

manifesto.body: Most software is a dashboard. It waits for you, stares at you, asks to be configured. We build the opposite: systems that watch themselves, heal themselves, and come back stronger every time something breaks. Chaos is scheduled. Verification is adversarial. Every fact ships with a receipt. Antifragile by design — with a character that stays.

work.heading: Four platforms. One doctrine.
work.sub: Everything below is real, in production, and drawn from the actual architecture. Open a case and pull the graph apart — every node is a running system.

pathcore.name: PathCore
pathcore.blurb: A hexagonal platform that treats failure as a training signal: chaos on a schedule, circuit breakers, cognitive AI workers — and MindView, a living map of the whole organism.
pathcore.headline: The system that heals itself.
pathcore.tagline: An infrastructure platform where failure is a training signal, not an incident.
pathcore.body1: PathCore is built as a strict hexagon — Core, Uncore, Un-uncore — where every capability lives behind a hard boundary. A chaos engine injects failure on purpose. Circuit breakers isolate the blast radius. Cognitive AI workers read the wreckage, diagnose the cause and propose the fix. The platform doesn't page a human at 3 a.m. — it retrains itself and moves on.
pathcore.body2: You watch all of it happen in MindView: a real-time graph of every service, worker and queue, streamed live over server-sent events. Deploys route through a failure-aware executor with automatic rollback; changes land through a merge queue in provably safe order. It is infrastructure with a nervous system — and a survival instinct.
pathcore.s3l: living map of the whole system

videolinker.name: VideoLinker
videolinker.blurb: Script in, broadcast-ready episode out. An 11-step pipeline, 60+ services and an autonomous agent wielding 59 tools — with a 60-rule QA gate before anything ships.
videolinker.headline: A film crew made of services.
videolinker.tagline: Script in — broadcast-ready episode out. No humans in the render path.
videolinker.body1: VideoLinker runs an 11-step production line: series bible, episode ideas, script, shot decomposition, keyframes, image-to-video, cloned-voice narration, word-timed captions, and a final FFmpeg composition with transitions, overlays and a mixed SFX bed. A dedicated GPU container upscales frames on the way through. Every episode faces a QA engine scoring it 0–100 against 60+ weighted rules — hook, pacing, variety, continuity — before it is allowed to exist.
videolinker.body2: Above the pipeline sits an autonomous agent: it plans the job, calls 59 tools across 12 tool servers, respects budget caps, and pauses for human approval only where you tell it to. Artifacts are content-addressed and deduplicated by hash. The whole factory is one API call wide.

frontdesk.name: FrontDesk
frontdesk.blurb: A public record of what things actually cost: AI writers compile, an adversarial agent refutes, a fidelity gate re-fetches every source — and a SHA-256 ledger makes history unrewritable.
frontdesk.headline: Every price has a receipt.
frontdesk.tagline: A public record of what things actually cost — sourced, dated, tamper-evident.
frontdesk.body1: FrontDesk is built on institutional distrust of its own content. Writer agents compile products and prices from published sources; a second, adversarial agent exists only to refute them. Whatever survives meets the fidelity gate, which re-fetches every cited page and refuses to ship any number that isn't literally there. The result is a corpus of 4,400+ entities where every fact carries a source URL and the date it was verified.
frontdesk.body2: A daily AI-free price scan writes into an append-only history, and a hash-chained ledger makes that history tamper-evident — you can't rewrite last month. The corpus fans out to 23,000+ citable pages, machine feeds built for AI readers, an MCP server with 19 tools, an open CC-BY mirror with a DOI, and a browser extension that overlays the price of record right on the store page.

relocating.name: Relocating
relocating.blurb: Open data distilled into 33 calculators, programmatic country corridors and a moderated live community — mirrored into 22 languages by its own translation pipeline.
relocating.headline: Moving countries, minus the guesswork.
relocating.tagline: Open data turned into calculators, corridors and a live community — in 22 languages.
relocating.body1: Relocating starts where the anxiety starts: what will it actually cost, what visa fits, how long until citizenship. A build-time ETL normalizes World Bank, weather and geographic data into 30+ datasets across 50 countries; a quality gate fails the entire build if a single dataset is inconsistent. From that spine, a page engine generates country corridors, comparisons and rankings, and 33 calculators run entirely client-side.
relocating.body2: The whole site is then mirrored into 22 languages by its own translation pipeline — self-hosted models, a versioned translation memory, and a hard build failure on any untranslated string. It ships as a fully static build to the edge: nothing to crash at runtime. Alongside the data lives City Chat, where every message passes AI moderation before it goes public, backed by EU-resident Postgres with row-level security and GDPR retention by construction.

approach.heading: How we build.
approach.i1b: We schedule chaos instead of fearing it. Circuit breakers, retries with memory, and AI workers that diagnose their own wreckage — every outage makes the system harder to kill.
approach.i2b: Nothing ships on one opinion. Writer agents are shadowed by refuting agents; fidelity gates re-fetch every source; QA engines score every artifact against dozens of rules before it exists in public.
approach.i3b: Every fact carries its source and its date. Append-only logs, hash-chained ledgers, tamper-evident history. If we can't prove it, we don't publish it.
approach.i4b: Software should not need a human staring at it. Our platforms deploy themselves, roll themselves back, translate themselves and moderate themselves — and page nobody.

studio.headline: An independent studio.
studio.p1: Autofract is an independent software studio. Four production platforms share one engineering doctrine: self-healing infrastructure, an autonomous video factory, a tamper-evident price record, and an open-data relocation hub — over a hundred services, designed, built and operated end to end.
studio.p2: Not VC-funded, not hiring. We build slowly, on purpose, for the long run.
